\section*{Editorial corrections and accuracy notes}
\noindent\textit{Annotation --- not part of the original text. Scope:
Chapter 7 introduction and SHORT EXPIRATIONS only (printed pp.~87--89;
PDF pp.~118--120). Register: \texttt{gatheral-07-s01-convert-call-012}.}\par\smallskip

\textbf{Applied material corrections (visible notes C1--C3 above).}
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{C1} (\texttt{gatheral-07-s01-convert-call-012-7099c8cc43};
printed p.~87, display after the \(dZ_2\) decomposition --- source error).
Book prints \(\alpha(\nu,t)\), \(\beta(\nu,t)\) although the text
explicitly specializes to \(\alpha,\beta\) independent of \(t\); (7.1)
uses \(\alpha(\nu),\beta(\nu)\), the display's own last term reads
\(\beta(\nu)\), and all later displays use \(\alpha(\nu),\beta(\nu)\).
Applied \(\alpha(\nu,t)\to\alpha(\nu)\), \(\beta(\nu,t)\to\beta(\nu)\).
\item \textbf{C2} (\texttt{gatheral-07-s01-convert-call-012-137d7900f2};
printed p.~88, lemma proof --- source error, coefficient). Book prints
``a roughly constant \(\beta(\nu_0)\)''; from (7.2) that slope is
\(\rho\eta\,\beta(\nu_0)\), and the proof's own formal display and (7.3)
both carry \(\rho\eta\). Inserted \(\rho\eta\); original wording recorded
in note C2.
\item \textbf{C3} (\texttt{gatheral-07-s01-convert-call-012-8d5d70a04c};
printed p.~89, closing paragraph --- source error, cross-reference). Book
prints ``derived earlier in Chapter~7 for the Heston model'' --- an
impossible self-reference (this is Chapter~7; the short-dated skew is
derived here for the first time). The Heston skew (3.19) was derived in
Chapter~3, as stated twice later in this chapter, and its \(T\to0\) limit
\(\rho\eta/2\) for \(\beta(\nu)=1\) matches (7.3). Changed to
``Chapter~3''.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Extraction repairs (silent in the document; not source errors).}
\begin{itemize}
\item Drop-cap ``F'' lost by MinerU in the chapter's opening word;
restored as ``From'' (drop cap visible on PDF p.~118).
\item End-of-proof tombstone (\(\sqcap\!\sqcup\), PDF p.~120) garbled to an
invalid character by MinerU; restored as \(\square\).
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Extraction disagreement resolved (log only; no mathematical
impact).} Figure 7.1 caption (printed p.~89): MinerU shows tildes on
\(\tilde{\sigma}^{2}_{BS}(k,T)\) and \(\tilde{\nu}_{loc}(0,0)\); the PDF
text layer shows none there (accents are routinely lost in jumbled caption
text, in contrast with extracted ``\(\tilde{x}\)'' in body text). Kept
MinerU's tildes, per the preferred structured extraction for mathematical
layout.

\textbf{Preserved as printed.} No punctuation after ``\(\beta(\nu)=1\)''
before ``we see'' (printed p.~89); both extractions agree; cosmetic, left
verbatim.

\textbf{Image-inspection wishlist.} Printed p.~89: Figure 7.1 caption
(confirm the two tildes) and the closing paragraph (confirm the missing
punctuation). Printed p.~88: proof sentence (confirm \(\rho\eta\) is
truly absent in print).

\textbf{Consistency checks passed.} \(\varphi=\sqrt{1-\rho^{2}}\) gives an
orthogonal decomposition \(dZ_2=\rho\,dZ_1+\varphi\,dZ_1^{*}\);
eliminating \(\sqrt{\nu}\,dZ_1 = dx + \frac{\nu}{2}\,dt\) reproduces the
following two displays. (7.2) follows from
\(\mathbb{E}[\nu+d\nu\mid dx]\) using \(\int_{0}^{t}\nu_s\,ds\approx\nu_0 t\).
The straight-line most-probable path \(\tilde{x}_t=x_T\,t/T\) gives
\(\int_{0}^{T}\tilde{x}_t\,dt=\frac{1}{2}x_T T\), hence the factor
\(\frac{1}{2}\) in (7.3). (7.3) agrees with the Medvedev--Scaillet
short-dated skew (7.6) later in this chapter via
\(b(\sigma)=\eta\,\beta(\sigma^{2})/2\), \(\sigma=\sqrt{\nu}\).

\smallskip
\noindent\textbf{Unresolved issues: none in this section.}

edits.old:
\noindent{\small\textbf{GLM unresolved issue (second-order coefficients in
(7.12)).} As printed, $J^{(3)}\to 3\rho\,\overline{\nu}^{\,2\phi}/(2\lambda^3)\neq 0$
as $t\to 0$ (its brace tends to $3$), whereas the braces of $J^{(1)}$ and
$J^{(4)}$ vanish as $t\to 0$. Since $\beta_0$ contains
$-\frac{1}{2}\,J^{(3)}/(\nu t^2)\,(1+\frac{1}{4}\nu t)$ and $\beta_2$ contains
$\frac{1}{2}\,J^{(3)}/(\nu^2 t^3)$, both would diverge (like $t^{-2}$ and
$t^{-3}$) as $t\to 0$. This contradicts the finite short-time limits implied
by the Medvedev--Scaillet expansion (7.5): for the Example-4 process (where
$b(\sigma)=\eta\sigma^{2\phi-1}/2$) the $k^2$ coefficient of implied variance
must approach the finite value
$\eta^2\overline{\nu}^{\,2\phi-2}\big[\tfrac{1}{12}+\rho^2\big(\tfrac{\phi-1}{6}-\tfrac{1}{16}\big)\big]$,
which contains no term linear in $\rho$, whereas the printed $\beta_2$ has no
$\rho$-independent term at all and its only $\rho$-linear piece is the
$J^{(3)}$ term. The quoted $J^{(3)}$ and/or the $\mathrm{O}(\eta^2)$
coefficients of (7.12) are therefore misprinted (in the book and/or this
transcription); the correct form cannot be recovered by local derivation
alone. Evidence needed: Lewis (2000), pp.~142--144 --- equation (3.14)
itself and the definitions of $J^{(2)}$, $J^{(3)}$, $J^{(4)}$ --- to verify
the $\mathrm{O}(\eta^2)$ coefficients. The first-order result used below is
unaffected.}\par
edits.new:
\noindent{\small\textbf{GLM unresolved issue, qualified by Codex source-image and local-limit checks [G7-Lewis].}
The source image at physical PDF 128 / printed 97 confirms the displayed
$J^{(3)}$ brace $3/2+\lambda t+2e^{-\lambda t}-e^{-2\lambda t}/2$;
it tends to $3$. For $\rho\ne0$ and nonzero volatility of volatility, positive
$\nu=\bar\nu$ and $\lambda>0$, its contribution to the displayed $\beta_2$
is of order $t^{-3}$. The other displayed terms cannot cancel it:
$J^{(1)}=O(t^2)$ and $J^{(4)}=O(t^3)$, so their contributions to $\beta_2$
are bounded. This is a substantive inconsistency in the printed formula,
not merely an OCR discrepancy. No corrected coefficient is invented here.
The earlier GLM claim that $\beta_0$ must also diverge is not independently
established: $J^{(2)}$ is not defined in this section, so cancellation there
has not been excluded. Lewis (2000), pp.~142--144, equation (3.14) and the
underlying $J^{(n)}$ definitions are needed to settle the precise correction.
The printed formulas remain available as flagged knowledge-base content;
the first-order calculation below is retained.}\par
